title: Calories you burn and calorie targets
rule: Resting calories use the Mifflin-St Jeor equation from weight, height, age and sex, or the Katch-McArdle equation when body fat is known (it uses lean mass, so it fits muscular people better). Daily calories are resting calories times an activity factor. A deficit of about 500 calories a day is the usual starting point for losing about 1 pound a week. Plans below about 1,200 calories a day (women) or 1,500 (men) should be supervised by a clinician. BMI is weight divided by height squared; for Asian adults the WHO expert consultation set lower action points (23 and 27.5).
confirm_with: your doctor or a registered dietitian
notes: Equations: Mifflin et al. 1990 (PubMed 2305711). Pregnancy extras from the National Academies energy DRIs. Asian BMI action points: WHO expert consultation, Lancet 2004 (PubMed 14726171). The NIH Body Weight Planner gives a more exact weight-loss curve. Not re-checked today.
